cohort: Pregnancies delivered at 40 weeks and 10 days or more at Federal Teaching hospital, Abakaliki, Nigeria, from January 2013 to December 2015.
finding: Post-date pregnancies were associated with increased rates of cesarean section, primarily due to labor dystocia, as well as neonatal sepsis, perinatal death, and postpartum hemorrhage.
mod_finding: Vaginal delivery and cesarean sections were the mode of delivery in 73.9% and 25.0% of women, respectively; Cesarean sections were mainly for labor dystocia (54.5%).
